events.title: Michael Servetus Burned at the Stake
events.description: The Spanish theologian and physician Michael Servetus was condemned as a heretic for rejecting the doctrine of the Trinity and infant baptism. He was burned at the stake just outside Geneva.
events.significance: His execution became a landmark case in the early debate over religious tolerance and freedom of conscience in Europe.

events.title: Philadelphia Is Founded
events.description: The city of Philadelphia was founded in Pennsylvania. It was established under William Penn, who had landed at New Castle in the Delaware Colony around this time on his way to the new settlement.
events.significance: Planned as a haven of religious freedom, Philadelphia grew into one of colonial America's leading cities and later hosted the nation's founding documents.

events.title: Birth of Theodore Roosevelt
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt was born in New York City. He became the 26th President of the United States and won the Nobel Peace Prize.
events.significance: Roosevelt shaped the modern presidency through conservation efforts, trust-busting and an assertive role for America on the world stage.

events.title: New York City Subway Opens
events.description: New York City's first subway line began operating, carrying passengers between Lower Manhattan and Harlem.
events.significance: The subway transformed urban life in the city and grew into one of the largest and busiest rapid transit systems in the world.

events.title: Turkmenistan Declares Independence
events.description: As the Soviet Union was collapsing, Turkmenistan declared independence. The Central Asian country had been a Soviet republic since 1925.
events.significance: It was one of the nations that emerged from the Soviet breakup, and the date is still celebrated there as Independence Day.
